To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the redox function of E10R is essential for the formation of disufide bonds of G4L, L1R and the F9L, and that G4L is an intermediate in a cytoplasmic disulfide bond pathway required for virion formation.
the E10R protein is required for virions to be assembled, and that E10R is part of a pathway in which G4LRSS → L1R and possibly also F9LSS → E10R, and G4LSS are intermediates.
the E10R, G4L, L1R and/or F9L disulphide bond pathway is required for virions to be assembled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the E10R, G4L, L1R and, F9L proteins in virion assembly and the identification of a novel pathway for the formation of disulphide bonds in vaccinia virus.
the identification of a novel disulfide bond pathway required for vaccinia virus morphogenesis.
the role of the G4LRSS → L1RSS pathway in virion assembly and provides evidence for a new function of the ERV1 family of redox proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E10R is required to form disulfide bonds between G4L and L1R and between G4L, L1R and/or F9L.
E10R is the redox enzyme responsible for the formation of disulphide bonds between the two cysteines of L1R, F9L and G4L and that the latter two proteins are required for virion formation.
E10R and G4L are essential for virus assembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E10R is required to oxidize G4L, which in turn oxidizes L1R and/or F9L, whose intramolecular disulphide bonds are required for virion morphogenesis.
a redox cascade involving the ERV1 family protein E10R and the G4L and L1R glutaredoxins is required for the formation of virion disulfide bonds.
the redox pathway involving E10R, G4L, and L1R and/or F9L is an important component of the vaccinia virion assembly pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the redox pathway is a critical component of virion assembly.
the E10R, G4L, and F9R proteins are required for virion formation, and the G4L protein is a disulfide bond intermediate of a cytoplasmic pathway required for virion disulfide bond assembly.
G4L, an essential viral glutaredoxin with a unique C-terminal domain, is an intermediate in a cytoplasmic disulfide bond pathway that is required for virions to form.
